item.description:
Fixed

  • Qwen dictation now uses the same greedy decoder as the official speech CLI.

The 2026-08-19.1 build stopped the memory balloon but still pasted mixed

garbage because Release builds were taking the slow repetition-penalty path.

Notes

  • Memory use from the 2026-08-19 leak remains fixed.
  • This build is Apple Silicon only. Qwen is dictation-only.

Fixed

  • Qwen dictation no longer runs MLX decode on the Swift cooperative thread

pool. That path turned short recordings into thousands of garbage tokens

and drove unified memory above 10 GB, so nothing useful was pasted.

  • Decoder token budget now follows clip length, so a one-second file cannot

emit a thousand tokens of junk.

Notes

  • This build is Apple Silicon only.
  • Qwen remains dictation-only. Meetings still use Parakeet or Soniox.

New

  • On-device Qwen3-ASR 0.6B for dictation. Pick it in Settings → Transcription

engine. It transcribes after you stop recording, fully on your Mac, with no

cloud upload. First use downloads about 1 GB of model weights.

Improved

  • Qwen now loads through a single shared runtime, so Settings download and

dictation cannot each keep a full copy of the model in memory.

  • Longer dictations are split into 15-second chunks instead of silently

truncating at the decoder token cap.

  • Settings only marks the Qwen model downloaded when the full weight set is

present, not a partial download.

Notes

  • This build is Apple Silicon only. The on-device Qwen engine uses MLX, which

cannot compile for Intel.

  • Qwen is for dictation, not meetings. Meetings still use Parakeet or Soniox.
  • Download the model in Settings before the first Qwen dictation. If the

weights are missing, dictation will ask you to download rather than stalling

on HuggingFace at stop.

  • Parakeet remains the default on-device engine. Meeting capture, history,

settings, permissions, and Keychain credentials remain compatible.

New

  • Paste as rich text. Turn it on in Settings → Language model and dictated

bullet points, numbered lists, and bold/italic text paste as real formatting

in apps that accept rich text, such as Slack, Notes, and Mail. Plain text is

always included as a fallback, so apps that only take plain text paste

exactly as before.

  • Vercel AI Gateway support, chosen per model. The model browser now offers

the Vercel AI Gateway catalog alongside OpenRouter — browse either, favourite

models from both, and mix them freely in one favourites list. Each request

automatically uses the gateway and API key belonging to the selected model.

Save your Vercel key in Settings → LLM Gateways.

Improved

  • Beeper response windows now mute instead of snoozing. Muting a sender stops

their messages entirely for the chosen duration — nothing is held back to

resurface later. Unmute early from the menu bar.

  • Multiple messages from the same sender now thread into the one response

window as they arrive, instead of stacking counters behind a single message.

  • Minimized response pills now show the chat or task title instead of just

"Beeper", "Hermes", or "Codex", and hovering shows a preview of the text

inside.

Notes

  • Model browsing and OpenRouter voice transcription continue to use your

OpenRouter key. Routing priority and reasoning options apply to

OpenRouter-routed models only.

  • Meeting capture, history, settings, permissions, and Keychain credentials

remain compatible.

Improved

  • Redesigned the recording overlay that appears when you start a dictation or a

command. It is now a more compact capsule with a centre-out equaliser that

expands from the middle as you speak, replacing the previous row of bars.

  • The overlay now animates. It grows out of a single dot when you press your

hotkey and collapses back into that same point when the recording ends,

instead of appearing and disappearing abruptly.

  • The audio visualiser now reacts to your voice far more accurately. It uses the

same metering as the meeting recorder, with headroom for close microphones, so

normal speech no longer pins the bars at full height with no visible movement.

  • The visualiser is now driven in step with the display refresh rather than on a

fixed timer, which removes the flicker that appeared while recording.

  • The live transcript preview is now slightly translucent so it reads as an

overlay on top of your work rather than a solid block.

Fixed

  • The live transcript preview no longer opens at full size. It previously kept

the height of your last dictation, so it appeared as a large empty box before

any text arrived. It now starts as a single line and grows as you speak.

  • Removed a faint grey rectangle that could appear behind the recording overlay.

Notes

  • Dictation, transcription, and insertion behaviour are otherwise unchanged.
  • Meeting capture, history, settings, permissions, and Keychain credentials

remain compatible.

Fixed

  • Fixed meetings getting stuck after you stop them. If the transcription service

closed its stream without confirming completion, the meeting stayed in its

"processing" state indefinitely — the red recording dot never cleared, and the

summary, retry, and export controls stayed unavailable. Finalization is now

bounded: if the service stalls, the transcript is recovered from the recorded

audio and the meeting completes normally.

  • Regenerating a meeting summary now also replaces a placeholder title. Meetings

that were recovered after an interruption kept a generic name such as

"Google Meet" with no way to generate a real one. Titles you have edited

yourself are never overwritten.

  • Meeting summaries now render Markdown tables as actual tables. Sections such as

Action items were previously shown as raw rows of pipe characters. Copying a

summary still produces Markdown, so pasting into Obsidian is unchanged.

Notes

  • Meeting capture, transcription, detection, and export behaviour are otherwise

unchanged.

  • Existing recordings, history, settings, permissions, and Keychain credentials

remain compatible.

Fixed

  • Fixed sustained high CPU usage during live meetings. The Meeting Companion's

Transcript / Context / Notes selector was re-measuring itself on every meeting

update — every streaming transcript token plus the one-second timeline — which

kept the main thread busy in a continuous layout pass.

  • As a knock-on effect, that busy main thread caused macOS to repeatedly disable

WonderWhisper's keyboard shortcut monitoring, so prompt hotkeys could stop

responding mid-meeting until they were re-enabled.

Diagnostics

  • Shortcut-monitoring interruptions now record whether macOS disabled them because

the app was too slow to respond or because of user input, so the two can be told

apart in logs.

Notes

  • Meeting capture, transcription, tab switching, keyboard navigation, and

accessibility behaviour are unchanged.

  • Existing recordings, history, settings, permissions, and Keychain credentials

remain compatible.

What's new

  • Minimized Beeper, Hermes, and Codex response windows now appear as compact, source-labelled pills instead of anonymous grey circles.
  • Each pill uses a distinct source icon and colour, with clear indicators for errors, reply recording, and sending.
  • Added polished hover and press feedback while preserving the existing response-window lifecycle and stacking behaviour.

Accessibility

  • Minimized response pills now expose descriptive restore labels and help text, with a full-size accessible click target.

Notes

  • Existing recordings, history, settings, permissions, and Keychain credentials remain compatible.

What's new

  • Beeper messages now arrive in a WonderWhisper response panel. The panel says what came in and what the keyword filter held back, with earlier and new counts stated separately rather than summed.
  • A burst of messages from one chat stays on a single panel that updates in place, instead of stacking a new window per message. The newest message is what you see and what you reply to.
  • Minimizing a panel no longer silences the chat. If a new message arrives from a chat you minimized, that same panel comes back to the front with the new message in it. Minimize puts the window away; Snooze is the only thing that puts the chat away.
  • Typing a reply holds the panel still. While you have a draft in the composer or a reply in flight, the body stops moving and the new-message count keeps climbing; the moment you clear the draft the panel catches up.
  • Added Snooze to Beeper panels. One click snoozes the chat for an hour; 15 minutes and Until morning are in the menu. A snoozed chat stays out of your way everywhere except the menu bar, which is also where you resume it early.
  • Added Open Beeper to jump straight to the app.
  • A failed text reply now keeps your words. The composer stays open, the failure is named in the status row, and Send becomes Retry. Previously a failed send looked exactly like a successful one: an empty composer.
  • Sending from the in-app composer with the agent off no longer destroys what you typed.

Fixes

  • ⇧⌘C now works the first time, without opening the menu that owns it.
  • The menu bar's snooze section rebuilds on every open, so the countdown is current and a resumed chat disappears immediately.
  • VoiceOver reads the Beeper status line as one sentence and names the Open Beeper button, instead of speaking the separator dots and an unnamed link.
  • A voice reply can no longer lose the message it was answering. While you are recording, Close and Snooze on that panel are disabled, and ⌘W, Escape and the window close button cannot dismiss it out from under the recording. Previously either one dropped the reply target, and the finished transcription went out unaddressed or, with several chats configured, to the wrong one. Close and Snooze work as normal once the reply is sending.

Notes

  • Existing recordings, history, settings, permissions, and Keychain credentials remain compatible.
  • Hermes and Codex response panels are unchanged.

What's new

  • Added Homebrew installation, so WonderWhisper can be installed from the terminal with `brew install --cask dkapo88/tap/wonderwhisper`.
  • Documented in-app updating: WonderWhisper checks for new versions daily, and you can check on demand from the app menu, the menu bar icon, or Settings.

Notes

  • Existing recordings, history, settings, permissions, and Keychain credentials remain compatible.
  • Updates are verified against the developer signature before installing, so macOS permissions carry over.

What's new

  • Added automatic updates. WonderWhisper now checks for new versions once a day and can download and install them for you, so you no longer need to fetch a disk image by hand. Updates are verified against the developer signature before installing, which means your macOS permissions carry over untouched.
  • Added Check for Updates to the WonderWhisper app menu, the menu bar icon, and Settings.

Notes

  • This is the first release with built-in updating. Future versions will offer themselves automatically from here.
  • Existing recordings, history, settings, permissions, and Keychain credentials remain compatible.
